why: The future-schema lock. A payload whose `version` exceeds this build's is real data a NEWER build wrote; reinterpreting it field by field or overwriting it destroys settings this build cannot represent. Dropping the guard makes the next ordinary change stamp a version-1 payload over it. Killed by settings.test.ts's 'does NOT overwrite a future-schema payload', which asserts the RAW bytes are unchanged after a setter runs. 1 of 62 across the two declared files -- deliberately narrow: this is one specific byte-level property, and a broader failure population would mean some other test had started depending on the lock incidentally.
